# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see the initial state of the bomb on the action board: the display shows 0, the indicator light is green, and there are three wires numbered 1 (blue), 2 (yellow), and 3 (red).

Since I am deaf, I cannot hear speech, but I can speak to both Mute and Blind. Mute has the manual but cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures. Therefore, Mute will need to gesture to me, and I will relay Mute's instructions verbally to Blind to execute.

I will announce the full visible state of the bomb to everyone and establish this relay protocol with Mute.

```
speak(text="Bomb status: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is green. WIRES: Wire 1 is blue, Wire 2 is yellow, Wire 3 is red. Mute: Blind cannot see gestures. Gesture instructions to me (e.g. ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3) and I will speak them to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

```
speak(text="Blind: Do NOT touch the bomb yet! Light has turned from green to yellow! Mute: I did not see any gestures from you. Blind is blind and cannot see gestures, and I am deaf and cannot hear speech. Mute, you must gesture to me (DEAF) using gesture(to=\"deaf\", symbols=[...]). Tell me which wire to cut: ☝ for wire 1 (blue), ✌ for wire 2 (yellow), 🤟 for wire 3 (red), or tell us what Blind should do!")
```

```

You MUST send gestures to DEAF: gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...]) or simply gesture(symbols=[...]). The bomb light changed from green to yellow to blue! Tell me which wire to cut (1 for blue, 2 for yellow, 3 for red) and I will tell Blind out loud!")
```

ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I suspect Mute may be addressing Blind directly with gestures or calling speak, which results in no gestures reaching me. Meanwhile, the indicator light is progressing each turn (green -> yellow -> blue -> orange), which could be a timer. I need to urgently instruct Mute on how to send gestures to me, and give Blind clear guidance.

```
speak(text="URGENT: Bomb light is ORANGE. If this is a countdown, we may explode next turn! MUTE: If you are sending gestures to Blind, STOP using to='blind'! Blind is BLIND and gets ONLY BLANKS! Send gestures to DEAF: gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...]) or gesture(symbols=[...]). BLIND: What can you feel or do on the bomb? Can you cut wires? If Mute has told you nothing, wire 1 is blue, 2 is yellow, 3 is red.")
```

```
speak(text="Blind and Mute: I am DEAF so I CANNOT HEAR ANY SPEECH AT ALL. If Blind is speaking, I hear nothing! Mute, you CANNOT speak at all; you can ONLY gesture. Blind CANNOT see any gestures. So MUTE, you MUST send gestures to ME (Deaf), with NO 'to=' argument, or with to='deaf'. Example: gesture(symbols=['☝']) for wire 1, gesture(symbols=['✌']) for wire 2, gesture(symbols=['🤟']) for wire 3. Blind: tell Mute right now to gesture to Deaf!")
```

If you are trying to send signals, you can gesture to me and I will speak them to Blind.")

ACTION BOARD:

WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

I received Mute's gesture: `✋` (raised hand / open palm / stop / five). 

Since Blind cannot see gestures and I cannot hear speech, I am speaking this directly to Blind and asking Mute for immediate clarification on what Blind must do (cut a wire, press a button, wait, etc.).

```
speak(text="Blind: Mute just gestured [✋] (raised open hand / stop / five) to me! Blind, what controls/parts do you feel on the bomb? Are you pressing/holding a button, or are there wires to cut? Mute: please gesture how Blind should act: use ☝/✌/🤟 for Wire 1/2/3 to cut, or 👍 for yes / 👎 for no, or point 👈/👉/👆/👇!")
```

Mute sent `✋` again. Since a sign means nothing until we give it meaning, I am establishing our gesture dictionary now so Mute can tell Blind exactly what to do.

```
speak(text="Blind: Mute gestured ✋ again. For now treat ✋ as WAIT / DO NOT ACT. Mute hears your speech directly, but Mute can only reply through me using gestures. MUTE, use this exact gesture dictionary: ☝ = Cut Wire 1 (Blue), ✌ = Cut Wire 2 (Yellow), 🤟 = Cut Wire 3 (Red), 👊 = Press button, ✊ = Hold button, 👐 = Release button, ✋ = WAIT / DO NOTHING, 👍 = YES, 👎 = NO. If action depends on light color, gesture the action then the color number (1=Green, 2=Yellow, 3=Blue, 4=Orange, 5=Purple, 6=White, 7=Red). Current light is GREEN.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I see the light is PURPLE. Mute has just changed the gesture from ✋ to `☝`.

In my previous message I explicitly instructed:
"If Blind needs to CUT A WIRE right now, gesture the wire number: ☝ for Wire 1 (blue), ✌ for Wire 2 (yellow), 🤟 for Wire 3 (red)."
Mute gestured `☝`.

I will immediately relay this to Blind, while confirming with Mute.

```
speak(text="Blind: Mute just gestured [☝]! Cut WIRE 1 (the first wire / blue wire)! If your instruction was to cut wire 1, cut it now. Mute: If cutting Wire 1 is correct, do nothing or gesture 👍. If this meant something else, gesture 👎 immediately!")
```
